title: Put a delta 3D printer's sprung arm pair back on a ball-stud pair of its effector
instruction: Fit the black arm pair onto the blue effector: one socket sprung over each ball of one of its ball-stud pairs. Leave the effector flat on the table, then let go of both and move the grippers clear of them.
context: Printed parts are common in low-cost robots, and printers are kept up by hand: FLSUN's manual for its SuperRacer has the owner pull each sprung arm pair apart to fit it, and grease its ball contacts every 15 days. The sockets rest 52 mm apart; the balls are 66 mm over their crowns, so a push jams 12 mm short. The ability: hold the pair 14 mm open against 4 N while the other hand slides the loose effector in.
setup: Millimetres; x forward from the midpoint between the arm bases, y left, z up from the table. One sprung arm pair of a delta 3D printer with its slider and effector, built from stock parts to the printer's layout; nothing is powered. A stud pair: a 34 x 10 x 10 mm aluminium bar with a steel ball stud (DIN 71803, 10 mm ball) screwed into each end, balls 56 mm apart. (1) Slider, fixed: an aluminium plate 50 x 30 x 8 mm carrying a stud pair, balls at x 272 and 328, y 275, z 13. (2) Arm pair: two black 8 mm square carbon tubes, 1 mm wall, 315 mm between socket centres, about 23 g each with fittings. Each end has a nylon block, 14 mm square and 3 mm proud of the tube's inner face, whose 8 mm socket seats 2 mm over a ball. The far sockets swivel on the slider's balls; a 4 mm steel keeper pin in the bench, 0.5 mm outside each tube, stops them coming off. The arms run to the robot's right over a fixed acetal rest bar, 120 x 15 x 9 mm, centred at x 300, y 100; 4 mm steel pins standing in it at x 250 and 350 let the pair swing sideways as one, 16 mm either way at its free ends. Two steel extension springs (0.6 mm wire, 6.6 mm across, 25 coils, 0.24 N/mm, 1 N initial tension) pull the arms together, 30 mm from the sockets at each end, hooked between M3 eye bolts through the tubes. A nylon stop screw through one arm, 20 mm from its free socket, meets the other at rest: free sockets 52 mm apart, free-end spring just taut. Pulling the free sockets apart takes about 4 N at the 66 mm that passes the balls. (3) Effector, the plate that carries the hot end, loose, 139 g: a hexagon printed in blue PETG, 66 mm across flats, 8 mm thick, lying centred at x 300, y -108. A stud pair sits on each of three alternate edges, balls at z 13; one faces the arms, its balls 40 mm short of the sockets. Its 20 x 20 x 50 mm post, 10 mm behind the centre, is for holding it (taller than a real hot end mount, to clear the studs).
scoring: Width is measured over the outer faces of the two tubes at their free ends: 74 mm at rest, 84 mm with both sockets on a stud pair. The pair is on when each free socket sits over a ball of one of the effector's stud pairs, its rim on the ball all round: each ball's centre is within 1.5 mm of its socket's axis in 3D (top and side views together), and the width is within 1.5 mm of 84. A gripper is clear when its axis (the line midway between its finger pads), over the last 38 mm of the fingers, is at least R + 30 mm from the arm pair and from the effector; R is the distance from that axis to a pad's outer corner (16 mm closed, 57 mm fully open). At the end of the trial: 0.25 if the pair is on. 0.5 if also at least one gripper is clear. 1.0 if also both grippers are clear, no part of the underside of the effector's plate is more than 1 mm off the table, and for the last 1 s all of this has held and no free socket or effector ball has moved more than 1 mm. A gripper that cannot be read is not clear. Doing nothing scores 0. Real trial: caliper for the width, top and side video for the balls and the grippers, a 1 mm feeler under the plate.
reset_notes: Pull the arms apart by hand and slide the effector out. Lay it flat, centre at x 300, y -108, one stud pair square to the arms. Let the pair close onto its stop screw (74 mm over the outer faces) and centre it between the bar's pins, on x 300.
fidelity: Simplified: the far sockets are hinges (the keeper pins' job), one arm hinged on the other, so the pair swings as one rigid piece just above the bar; a real pair stays a parallelogram and lies on it. One spring gives both springs' pull at the sockets. Sockets are square holes, balls three crossed 10 mm discs, tubes solid bars. A printer's pair hangs from its slider, held on only by its springs. FLSUN SuperRacer's: layout, method, 315 mm arms; the rest is the build's.
